trans.sense: pertaining to the moments before death

examples.text: The dying dog was put out of his misery with a single shot!
The battlefield was littered with the dead and dying.
The face of the dying man in the lingchi video monotonously evokes Maria Falconetti in Carl Theodor Dreyer ’s 1928 “Passion of Joan of Arc.”
examples.ref: 2007 July 25, Roberta Smith, “Figures Moving as if in a Trance Across an Isolated, Lawless Island”, in The New York Times, archived from the original on 26 Nov 2022:

glosses: Approaching death; about to die; moribund.

examples.text: In the dying moments of daylight I glimpsed a sail on the horizon.
The dieselisation of this line has not been, as is sometimes the case, a means of reviving a dying branch, but an improving hand to a healthy service.
examples.ref: 1957 April 15, P. J. Norris, “The Watford-St. Albans Branch”, in Railway Magazine, page 281:

examples.text: Just as with other recent reports by various bodies on HS2 and the ticket office closures, the National Audit Office's effort on the rail reform process is a devastating exposé of the failings and floundering of a dying administration that has failed to understand the value of having an efficient rail network.
examples.ref: 2024 March 20, Christian Wolmar, “NAO report highlights lack of clarity and purpose”, in RAIL, number 1005, page 34:

glosses: Declining, terminal, or drawing to an end.

examples.text: His dying words were of his mother.

glosses: Pertaining to death, or the moments before death.
